key_insight: SEM-DNN identifies contemporaneous bidirectional causal effects by learning nonlinear simultaneous equations with feature-dependent variances, using conditional covariance diagonalization to recover the true interaction coefficients.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical causal inference tool for systems with mutual feedback and no valid instruments, such as coupled sensors, markets, and autonomous control loops.
method: Jointly fits nonlinear structural mean functions and heteroscedastic variances with a diagonal Gaussian quasi-likelihood.
Uses the simultaneous-system Jacobian plus conditional residual covariance structure to identify reciprocal effects.
Relies on zero-mean, conditionally uncorrelated shocks with nonproportional variances to diagonalize residual covariance across covariates.
evidence_signal: Monte Carlo studies and a cereal scanner-data application show improved recovery of structural effects and diagnostic checks for identification strength, residual diagonalization, variance calibration, and optimization sensitivity.
watch_item: Training is computationally heavier than alternatives, and the causal interpretation depends on strong assumptions about shock structure and invariance of the underlying mechanisms.
paper_title: Learning Bidirectional Causal Interactions with Heteroscedastic Neural Networks
